summary: Develop practical AML/CFT reporting, case-file, and testimony skills through scenario-based exercises. Explore the five-day course.
lede: AML/CFT reporting training helps investigators and reporting analysts turn suspicious-activity alerts into clear, traceable case records. It covers assessing alerts and transactions, mapping beneficial ownership and relationships, and building chronologies with indexed evidence. Participants practise drafting and reviewing suspicious transaction report narratives and preparing testimony notes, while distinguishing observed facts from analysis.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who prepare, review, or explain AML/CFT investigations and reporting. It suits intermediate practitioners with some exposure to transaction monitoring, customer due diligence, or financial crime casework.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with AML/CFT compliance, transaction monitoring, customer due diligence, or financial crime investigations is recommended. No coding is required. Bring a laptop for spreadsheet-based exercises; course datasets and templates can be provided for practice.
